entries.title: API answers 401 Unauthorized
phrasings: the API returns 401 unauthorized
my API key is not accepted
invalid api key error from the REST API
a 401 error when calling the Blotato API
getting unauthorized from GET /v2/users/me/accounts
my key doesnt work, it says unautorized
which header do I put the API key in
every endpoint answers 401 even with a new key
not_this: the AI connector says invalid API key or auth session
my API key leaked, how do I make a new one
unauthorized when I log in to the Blotato website
entries.opening: Let's check the key, one step at a time.

steps.text: A 401 means Blotato did not accept the key.
Copy the full key again from Settings > API, including any = at the end.

cite.quote: Copy the full key, including any trailing `=` characters.

steps.text: Send it in the blotato-api-key header.

cite.quote: Include the key in the `blotato-api-key` header of each request.

steps.text: Test it with one read-only call: GET https://backend.blotato.com/v2/users/me/accounts.
A plan problem looks different: it answers 403 with a message about the subscription, not 401.

entries.next: Run that one read-only call and tell me the status code you get.
entries.proof: You will know it worked when that call answers 200. An empty list still counts: it means no social accounts are connected yet.

entries.title: "Too many requests" from a workflow
phrasings: too many requests error
rate limit exceeded when publishing
my workflow fails with 429
the service is receiving too many requests from you
how many posts can I send per minute through the API
n8n gets rate limited when posting lots of videos
polling the post status too often gives 429
too many request eror from blotato
checking the status over and over gets rate limited
not_this: the daily post limit for one social account
how many posts per day for one account
entries.opening: Your workflow is sending faster than Blotato accepts. The fix is to slow it down.

steps.text: That message means too many requests in one minute. Publishing and media uploads each allow 30 a minute.

cite.quote: Rate limit exceeded. Upload Media: 30 requests/minute. Publish Post: 30 requests/minute.

steps.text: Stop sending to that step, and if the error gives a time to wait, wait that long.

cite.quote: Wait for the retry interval when the response supplies one.

steps.text: Before you run it again, check which posts already went out, so none are sent twice.

cite.quote: Retain the submission ID, inspect existing work

steps.text: Then send fewer posts at a time when you turn the workflow back on.

cite.quote: Reduce concurrency and request frequency before resuming.

entries.next: Check which posts already went out, then turn the workflow back on with fewer at a time.
entries.proof: You will know it worked when the workflow runs through with no "too many requests" errors.

entries.title: Post to a LinkedIn company Page instead of a profile
phrasings: post to a LinkedIn company page instead of my personal profile
how do I publish to our LinkedIn business page with the API
my LinkedIn posts go to my profile, not the company page
which id do I use for a LinkedIn organization page
LinkedIn page id and account id for the API
account not found when I use our LinkedIn page id as the account id
can i post on linkdin brand page not my own profile
not_this: how many accounts does a LinkedIn page count as on my plan
where do I find my Facebook page id
does each LinkedIn page count as a separate account
how many social accounts can I connect on my plan
if I connect a linkedin company page does it count toward my starter account limit
post to a LinkedIn company page from the web app
entries.opening: Yes, you can. It takes two ids instead of one.

steps.text: A LinkedIn company Page needs both your account id and the Page id.

cite.quote: For LinkedIn company pages, you need both an accountId and a pageId.

steps.text: Get the account id from GET /v2/users/me/accounts, then the Page id from GET /v2/users/me/accounts/{accountId}/subaccounts.

cite.quote: Use `GET /v2/users/me/accounts` to get the accountId, then `GET /v2/users/me/accounts/{accountId}/subaccounts` to get the pageId.

steps.text: Put the account id in post.accountId and the Page id in post.target.pageId.

cite.quote: Pass accountId in `post.accountId` and pageId in `post.target.pageId`.

steps.text: Watch for one common mix-up: the Page id going where the account id belongs.

cite.quote: A common mistake is passing the pageId where accountId is expected.

steps.text: If pageId is left out, the post goes to your personal profile.

cite.quote: Omit to post to personal profile.

entries.next: Check both ids are in the right fields, then send one test post.
entries.proof: You will know it worked when the test post shows on the company Page, not on your profile.

entries.title: Schedule lookup answers 500 "invalid input syntax for type bigint"
phrasings: GET /v2/schedules/{id} gives a 500 invalid input syntax for type bigint
the schedule lookup fails with a bigint error
invalid input syntax for type bigint
a 500 bigint error when I update a schedule with the id from the docs
a schedule id like sch_ answers a server error
entries.opening: Thank you for the exact error. I could reproduce it.

steps.text: Same result here: {evidence}
Our docs show schedule ids like "sch_abc123" in their examples.
The error says the server expected a number (a bigint), so the id from the docs example will not work there.
I am passing this to a person on the team, with the steps to reproduce it and a suggested change to the docs.

entries.next: Copy an id from your own GET /v2/schedules list, try that, and tell me what you get.
entries.proof: Still open: whether the API or the docs example is the one to change. A person on the team decides.

escalate.why: The API and the docs disagree. Only the founder can say which one is right.

causes.text: The schedule endpoints expect a number id, while the docs examples show a text id.
The customer copied an id from a docs example instead of from their own GET /v2/schedules list.

ruledOut.text: A bad key: a bad key answers 401, not 500.

docEdit.add: Schedule ids are numbers, sent as strings. Copy the id from GET /v2/schedules. An id that is not a number is rejected.
docEdit.note: Seen on the real API on Nov 15, 2026 (GET /v2/schedules/<text id> answered 500 "invalid input syntax for type bigint"). The OpenAPI file types the id as a plain string. Confirm with the founder before publishing.
